_comment: Six-step journey for the Gas Pipe Sizing Workbook store screenshots, replayed by scripts/media-capture.mjs and framed by scripts/store-kit.py. Every coordinate was measured from the live view hierarchy (uiautomator dump) of the signed release build on the Medium_Phone AVD at 1080x2400 / 420dpi, not guessed. Re-measured after the app gained ads, a one-time Pro unlock and the Calculator/Cases/Guide bottom navigation: the previous coordinates belonged to a layout that no longer exists.
_why_the_waits: Each step is executed back to back with no settling time, and the runner waits only one second after launching the app. Compose needs longer than that to draw the form, needs a moment between focusing a field and receiving text or the entry is dropped, and needs a moment between a segmented-button tap and the recomposition that follows it before the next tap is computed against the new layout. The waits below are load-bearing, not padding: without the leading one the material field silently stays empty.
_why_the_clears: The app persists the entered case across process death on purpose, so a field can already hold text when a run starts. Typing into a non-empty field appends: this is exactly how a stray '2' became the leading character of the material field ('2Schedule 40 steel') in one run. Each clear step puts the caret at the end and deletes what is there, which makes every entry idempotent instead of a function of the previous run.
_why_the_expects: A screenshot is a claim about the product. Each shot declares the readings that must be on screen for it to be honest, and media-capture dumps the live view hierarchy before AND after the shutter and asserts that each reading is the text of the field its label names, so the claim is about the photographed frame rather than a screen read seconds earlier. This is the only check in the pipeline that reads the artifact back: verify-slot --strict-store only proves a PNG exists at the right size, which is how six captures of IME autocorrect gibberish once passed as this app's entire store presence. Two rules make an entry falsifiable, and media-capture refuses the journey at load time when either is broken: a reading must be at least 2 characters, because a bare '4' or 'A' is satisfied by almost any screen; and it must name the field it belongs to, so a value typed into the wrong field cannot pass. Field captions ('Material or system', 'Fitting quantity') are still deliberately not listed as readings - on their own they render regardless of what was entered and are incapable of failing - they appear only as the label that identifies the field a real reading must be found in.
_why_the_values_are_not_round: The fitting allowance is 12 x 5.5 ft, so shot-06 asserts 'Fitting allowance: 66.00 ft' and '106.00 ft total run'. Round inputs (4 x 5) let a wrong computation agree with a right one by coincidence; 66.00 and 106.00 can only appear if the quantity, the per-fitting length and the developed length were all read from the fields they were typed into. 1-character entries ('4', '5', 'A', '2') cannot be asserted at all - media-capture refuses them as unfalsifiable - so the citation's table and row are asserted where the app echoes them in full, in 'Capacity provenance: CodeCitation(codeAndEdition=2024, table=A, row=2)' on shot-06, and only the edition (2024) is asserted in its own field on shot-03.
_why_imperial_then_metric_then_imperial: shot-04 is captured in metric and shot-05 switches back to imperial, so the same case is photographed in both unit systems. The switch is not free to fake: the canonical values stay imperial, shot-06 asserts '100.00 MBH required' and '106.00 ft total run' (40 ft developed + 66 ft of fittings) after the round trip, so a conversion that drifted would fail its own expectations instead of shipping. The unit segmented row is one of the two places where the tap target is the item centre (x=317 for the left item, 762 for the right), not the text centre: the selected item grows a check icon that moves its label off centre.
_why_the_scroll_gestures_repeat: Only the two extremes are stable, so every capture scrolls to an extreme with more swipes than it needs (extra swipes at an edge are no-ops) rather than to a distance. shot-02 is the exception, because the fitting fields sit below the fold at the top and above it at the bottom: it reaches the top extreme, then walks down in five fixed slow drags (300 px over 2600 ms each) and taps the boxes measured at that offset. Those drags are a primitive, not a preference. A fast flick lands wherever its fling ends: the same 1100 px flick that settled at one offset during measurement settled 682 px away in a capture run, because the fling inherits the velocity of the swipe before it, and that moved both taps into the gaps between fields - '12' was dropped entirely and '5.5' overwrote the developed length. A drag slow enough to stay under the platform's minimum fling velocity (300 px over 2600 ms is about 115 px/s against a 131 px/s threshold) has no fling to inherit: repeated twice from the top extreme it reproduced the same offset within 11 px, which a 168 px-tall field absorbs.
_preconditions: Target the release build. The debug variant carries a .debug applicationId suffix, so capturing it would photograph a package that never ships: node scripts/prepare-release.mjs --slot pipe-sizing, then adb install -r dist/pipe-sizing-<version>-release.apk

The release APK must be the minified artifact as built, because the checked-in app/proguard-rules.pro carries a load-bearing keep rule for Room's reflectively constructed database (androidx.work's WorkDatabase, pulled in by the ads capability). Without it the app builds, passes every gate and every unit test, and dies in androidx.startup before the first frame; media-capture then blocks on the first shot with nothing on screen to read. If the app crashes at launch, the rule was lost, not the coordinates.
Measured on the Medium_Phone AVD at 1080x2400 / 420dpi. Screens are captured at 1080x2400, so the phone assets are framed from a 2400px-tall source rather than 1920.

media-capture enforces the rest itself now: it runs 'pm clear' so the first shot cannot inherit the previous run's case, and it retries 'ime disable' until the enabled list is actually empty, because a live keyboard autocorrects typed values ('psig' became 'Paige') and rescrolls the form out from under these coordinates.

No interstitial can appear during a run: the free tier offers one every third evaluation, and this journey performs at most one computed evaluation (shot-06), with shot-05's refusal not counting as a completed evaluation.

The tablet assets are framed from these same phone captures rather than captured on a tablet device; no tablet AVD exists on this machine. Play treats large-screen assets as a claim about the large-screen experience, so this is disclosed in store/review-notes.md and the slot README instead of being passed off as a tablet capture.

shots.body: Switch to metric: the same readings, re-expressed rather than reinterpreted.

shots.title: Missing inputs are named
shots.body: A method-required reading that was never recorded is refused by name, not assumed.
